data.content_ref: inline:The dilemma dissolves if we view the preference as a pragmatic convention of the scientific game rather than an epistemic claim about the world. Just as a chess player prefers a move that has worked against grandmasters in the past without believing the rules of physics have changed, scientists prefer corroborated theories as a constitutive rule of the practice. This stance avoids induction entirely but costs science any claim to describing reality progressively, reducing it to a self-consistent language game where 'survival' is merely a scorecard internal to the community.
